panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (A, B, C, D, E). A: Panel A of a CT scan identifies a highly absorbent foreign body lodged at the left inferior lobar bronchus, directly fulfilling the criteria for foreign body aspiration. B: Panel B of the CT scan demonstrates infiltrative opacities extending from the foreign body site to the periphery, a recognized complication or secondary effect of foreign body aspiration. C: Panel C documents the absence of high-attenuation mucus within the infiltrative opacities, which is a specific diagnostic finding used to characterize the aspiration event. D: Panel D of the CT scan shows club-shaped opacities, consistent with bronchial mucus plugs, a common complication associated with airway foreign body aspiration. E: Panel E documents the absence of high-attenuation mucus within the club-shaped opacities, providing crucial diagnostic information regarding the nature of the obstructing material.

panels.rationale: The panel shows an FDG PET-CT image demonstrating a hypermetabolic focus in the right hemithorax. The caption and text confirm this focus corresponds to an endobronchial soft tissue nodule, suggesting a suspected foreign body aspiration. This corresponds to the configured disease 'airway_foreign_body_aspiration'.

in_text_mentions: A hybrid 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography-computed tomography (18F-FDG PET-CT) was performed to evaluate the metabolic activity of the lesion. A 1.2 x 1.7 cm hypermetabolic focus with a standardized uptake value (SUVmax) of 7.2 was identified in the right hemithorax, corresponding to an endobronchial soft tissue nodule in the right bronchus intermedius (Figures 5, 6). Findings raised concern for a slowly growing endobronchial malignancy in this patient at high risk for malignancy. No additional hypermetabolic foci or FDG-avid lymph nodes were visualized.
